title: Flat resolutions under ringed slice extension
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ be a ringed site small in the fixed module universe, with $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $V\in\mathcal C$. Use the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/V,R|_V)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], total cochain tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $e_!$ be sheafification of the direct-sum extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $P$ is a possibly unbounded K-flat complex of $R|_V$-modules, then $e_!P$ is K-flat over $R$. If every term of $P$ is flat (tensoring with that term is exact), every term of $e_!P$ is flat. A termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ remains one after applying $e_!$. For strict inverse sequences, these assertions apply objectwise to complexes of towers [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; in particular an objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement remains an objectwise flat-term K-flat replacement, with its original strict transition maps. No boundedness, quasi-compactness or regularity assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Use the K-flat preservation conjunct of ringedOpen_totalTensor_kFlat directly. Its source and target are precisely the complexes and independent-coefficient K-flat predicates in this statement. No new total-tensor or signed-interchange argument is required here.

Fix a term M=P^i. Presheaf braiding followed by the inverse of the shared siteTensorRightIso, whiskered with the forgetful functor and sheafification, identifies the functor SM (forget, tensor on the left with M.val, sheafify) with siteSheafTensorRight M. Thus SM is exact by flatness. Set L=e_! and T=j^*. Restrict the natural projection isomorphism ringedSlice_extension_tensor to pairs (M,N) as N varies. Its components identify T followed by SM and L with the analogous presheaf-tensor-and-sheafification functor SN for L M. Its naturality is the projection-formula naturality at (id_M,f), simplifying the tensor identity map. Restriction, SM and extension are exact, hence SN is exact by transport across this natural isomorphism. Apply the same presheaf comparison for L M to conclude exactly IsFlatOnSite (L M). Repeat for every i. The construction works for zero modules and arbitrary slice objects; no uniqueness of maps to U or boundedness is used.

Install the canonical sheafification and locally bijective-equivalence witnesses already used by ringedOpenQuasiIso. The image chain-map component is definitionally L.map(q.f i). Its epimorphism follows from preservation of finite colimits by L. Exactness of L gives preservation of homology; apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesHomology to q and L. This proves the image quasi-isomorphism with the unchanged existing homology theory.

For a strict tower P and its resolution map q apply the preceding three conclusions to P.obj n and q.app n at each n. The output tower is definitionally P postcomposed with the complex extension functor, and whiskerRight q has components exactly the images of q.app n. Thus the original strict transitions and their commutation equations are retained automatically. No additional assertion about homology or epimorphisms in the tower category is needed for these objectwise conclusions.
